newsitem.title: FINLAND: U.S., Russian presidents meet for summit.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Russian presidents meet for summit.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin met for their summit in Helsinki on Thursday, and Clinton expressed optimism about the outcome of their talks despite tensions over NATO enlargement.

Clinton, Yeltsin and Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari sat in a row of ornate chairs for photographs in the presidential palace near the city's icy waterfront before moving on to their first session of talks over dinner.
"I think we will work something out," Clinton said when asked by reporters how he thought the summit would go.
Yeltsin struck a similarly optimistic note earlier on Thursday on arrival, saying he hoped for a compromise that would preserve the U.S.-Russian partnership.
Clinton, who is temporarily wheelchair-bound after an accident and surgery last week, said he was pleased to see Yeltsin back on form after months of illness.
"I'm glad to see President Yeltsin looking so fit and well," Clinton said.
